question: True or false: in the first 100 million primes, a prime's last digit tells you nothing about the next prime's last digit?
answer: False. After a prime ending in 1, the next ends in 1 only 18.5% of the time, against 25% if the digits were independent; it ends in 3 or 7 about 30% of the time. Every final digit shows the same reluctance to repeat, a pattern explained in 2016 by a conjecture still unproved.
move: Random-looking is not the same as independent; check what follows what.
trap: Primes look random, so one's final digit should say nothing about the next.
reference: Lemke Oliver & Soundararajan, Unexpected biases in the distribution of consecutive primes, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA, 2016
